title: Start in 60 minutes
intro: Don’t read the whole notebook. Get a thin harness into Cursor in about an hour — then come back for the philosophy.
promise: When you finish you have: two fail-closed rules, one on-demand skill, one signed pattern, and a tenure clock. That’s enough to stop the next stupid burn.

steps.title: Download the pack
steps.why: Empty templates invite dithering. This pack is already named and filled with boring defaults you can rename.
steps.do: Download the zip (or browse the files). Unzip next to a scratch project — or into a small git repo you control.
steps.proof: You can see README.md and a .cursor/ tree on disk.

steps.title: Drop files where Cursor loads them
steps.why: A harness that lives only in chat dies when the chat dies.
steps.do: Copy the pack’s `.cursor` folder into your project root (prefer project-local). Open the folder in Cursor and Reload Window if rules don’t show yet.
steps.proof: Cursor sees the two .mdc rules and the example-domain-task skill.

steps.title: Rename the skill to your real job
steps.why: Generic skills don’t fire. Trigger nouns must match how you talk.
steps.do: Edit skills/example-domain-task/SKILL.md: change the name, description triggers, When/Do steps, and Proof of done to one task you do weekly.
steps.proof: You can say the trigger phrase out loud and it matches the description.

steps.title: Keep the two P0 rules always-on
steps.why: Secrets in chat and silent outbound are the burns that don’t forgive.
steps.do: Read both rules. Change the wording if you must, but keep alwaysApply: true. Do not add a third always-on rule today.
steps.proof: You can explain each rule in one sentence to a colleague.

steps.title: Sign off one pattern
steps.why: Unsigned patterns are just opinions. Sign-off is what makes Kaizen real.
steps.do: Open patterns/WORKING-PATTERNS.md. Keep lean-tool-sessions as signed-off, or replace it with a failure you had this month. Write the problem in one line.
steps.proof: The table has exactly one signed-off row that matches a real incident.

steps.title: Freeze a tenure clock
steps.why: Without a start date, every demo invents a heroic timeline.
steps.do: Edit clocks.json: set harness.start to today’s date (ISO). Leave the other clocks or delete them.
steps.proof: A date you trust is on disk — not only in a slide.

steps.title: Run one real task
steps.why: The harness is only real under load.
steps.do: Ask the agent to do the skill’s task. Require the proof checklist. If it skips a gate, stop and tighten the rule — don’t shrug.
steps.proof: You have a short note of what changed and how you verified it.

steps.title: Schedule a tiny Hansei
steps.why: Without reflection the pack becomes folklore in a week.
steps.do: Put a 15-minute calendar block in seven days: keep / amend / retire on the pattern and skill. Link this site’s Learning section if you want the longer loop.
steps.proof: The calendar (or ticket) exists. You are done for today.

done.title: Done when
checks: Pack installed where Cursor loads it
Two always-on P0 rules still always-on
One signed-off pattern with a real problem line
One task run with proof — not a plan alone

next: When this feels boring (good), read the Playbook or Learning sections. Skip what you don’t need.
